cards.hearing: You may hear that police are investigating a possible bomb threat at a UK air base used by U.S. forces, with a possible Iran link, and that oil prices jumped on the news this morning.
cards.why: Oil is the raw material behind gas and diesel, so when it jumps, that can eventually show up at the pump and on delivery costs for the things we buy.
cards.but: But headlines like this move markets fast in the morning and often fade just as fast once more facts come in.
cards.story: Picture seeing storm clouds on the horizon during a picnic. You do not pack up the whole basket over a cloud. You watch, you stay put, and most days the rain passes without ever reaching the blanket.
say: We saw this headline too, and your plan did not move because of it.
One tense morning is not a reason to change a long-term plan.

cards.hearing: You may hear that the Fed, which sets short-term interest rates, just raised rates for the first time in years, and people are asking what that means for their wallet.
cards.why: Higher rates can mean a pricier car loan, credit card, or new mortgage, though savings accounts can also start paying a bit more over time.
cards.but: But this kind of move doesn't rewrite a plan built for decades, not one headline.
cards.story: Think of it like turning a thermostat up one notch. The room changes a little, but the house, and the life you built in it, stays the same.
say: We build plans that expect rate moves like this one.
One rate change doesn't change your long-term plan.
